findings.issue: Restore “partial pressure” instead of the broader “pressure” in the graph label.
findings.evidence: The reference entry specifies concentration or partial pressure versus time. The table cell is otherwise correct, but the more precise label avoids suggesting total pressure, which can remain constant throughout the approach to equilibrium when a gas reaction has no change in total gas moles.

findings.issue: “Both directions always occur” is an overgeneralization.
findings.evidence: The intended correction—that the existence of two directions does not establish equilibrium—is right, and equilibrium does require equal rates. However, the sources do not establish that both rates are nonzero at every instant. As standard chemistry, an initial reactant-only mixture can have a zero reverse rate until some product forms. Use “both directions can occur” or “the existence of both directions does not mean their rates are equal.”
